A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTRA research by the same authors. All 16 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including Appendices A–D, are readable. Equations, experiments, figures, and tables can be matched despite extensive restructuring.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original MIS, diverse bipartite matching, and MaxCut experiments, including solution quality, diversity, and runtime results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain original empirical studies and report additional baseline comparisons, diversity measurements, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The tensor-output GNN, summed objectives, and standard-deviation diversity penalty are retained. However, v2 Section 3 specifies positive-to-negative annealing, reversing v1's stated direction while retaining its objective sign, negative initialization, and Appendix A theory. The PDFs therefore do not resolve whether the procedure changed or the revised description is inconsistent.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MIS on small and large random-regular graphs, the same 27 CORA-derived DBM instances with Matching-1 and Matching-2 variants, and the same seven Gset MaxCut instances. The multi-instance DBM study is retained. The molecular-design example added to v2 is motivation, not an evaluated task.

E2.justification: V2 Figures 2–3 add PI-GNN to the MIS and DBM penalty-sweep comparisons, which previously compared CTRA primarily against CRA-PI-GNN. Figures 5–6 add greedy search and explicit repeated-run PI-GNN/CRA comparisons for solution diversity. RUN-CSP remains in the relocated Gset table, so that comparator was not removed.

E3.justification: V2 adds average ApR and normalized pairwise-Hamming DScore, assessing collections of 300 MIS or 1,000 G14 solutions against repeated baseline runs. It also reports parameter costs and revises the displayed shot-scaling sweep from up to 2^14 shots to approximately 10^3. These substantially expand the evaluation design; most stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds MIS PCA analysis, baseline PCA comparisons, and parameter-count scaling, and expands diversity-penalty sensitivity analysis using average quality, DScore, and runtime. The earlier MIS distance/maximum-ApR analysis and G14 distance histograms are retained in Appendix D. The G14 maximum-ApR-versus-penalty curve from v1 Figure 7 is replaced by different summary comparisons.

E5.justification: Five-seed standard-deviation reporting remains for penalty sweeps, runtime curves, and multi-instance experiments. V2 newly specifies different-seed baseline repetitions of 300 runs for MIS and 1,000 for G14, distinct from CTRA's multiple outputs within one run. Reporting is uneven: the new G14 table displays no uncertainty despite its caption claiming standard-deviation errors.

E6.justification: V2 adds many runtime, parameter-count, average-ApR, and DScore entries; Figure 5 reports MIS CTRA at nu=0.2 with average ApR 0.936 and DScore 0.260. MIS penalty-sweep curves are revised. V1's DBM CRA runtime summary of 165,291±2,851 seconds is replaced by variant-specific reports of 213,612±5,132 and 208,141±903 seconds. These are revised reports, without establishing same-setting performance gains. The seven-instance Gset scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.2, and the Appendix A proofs are substantially retained. V2 removes v1's explicit differentiability/access assumption, introduces the DScore definition and an O(S^2)-versus-O(S) computation argument, and expands the entropy formulation. Its newly stated odd-alpha domain conflicts with the retained even-alpha assumptions, rather than providing a resolved theoretical revision.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains efficient generation of penalty-diversified and heterogeneous, renamed variation-diversified, solutions. V2's introduction and conclusion explicitly extend solution-quality superiority claims to greedy algorithms and emphasize parameter counts and runtime comparable to single-solution UL solvers. These broaden retained claims without introducing a new central research objective.

C2.justification: V2 more strongly attributes efficiency and quality gains to shared representations, whereas v1 presents this mechanism as a conjecture. It adds explicit quality/diversity/runtime tradeoffs against greedy search and attributes runtime growth to GPU memory limits. The expanded distinction between learning from datasets and optimizing individual instances also introduces substantive applicability and generalization limitations.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses V100 GPU use, a fixed MIS penalty of lambda=2, and the NetworkX and Mehta greedy implementations, including a code citation. Most architecture, optimizer, stopping, and rounding details already appeared in v1 Section 4.1 and are relocated to Appendix C. The new disclosures do not establish that those underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises positioning around learning from historical instances versus individual-instance optimization, and offline, online, and simultaneous diversity methods. It adds annealing work by Sun et al. and Sanokowski et al., simulated annealing, and evolutionary optimization comparisons. Several earlier references disappear, including Toenshoff et al. despite the retained RUN-CSP results.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. Heterogeneous solutions become variation-diversified solutions; related work moves before experiments; problem descriptions and implementation material move into expanded appendix subsections. This is substantial rewriting and reorganization beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, redraws the overview around shared representations and post-selection, and introduces combined table-and-plot displays for the principal experiments. It adds an objective-function table and PCA displays, redraws scaling plots, and relocates retained analyses and the Gset table into the appendix.

improvement.justification: The added greedy/PI-GNN comparisons and joint quality, diversity, and cost summaries strengthen empirical assessment. However, v2 introduces conflicting annealing instructions, and Figure 3 reports Matching-1 CTRA maximum ApR as 0.883 while its accompanying grid shows near-optimal solutions. These inconsistencies affect the central procedure and interpretation of results. The PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction when weighing the useful additions against the new reliability problems.
